Megan / Aurelius team —

Attached are the artifacts we discussed. Summary first, then attachments listed below.

High-level summary:
- Ephemeral keys: Redwood issues short-lived session keys derived from a customer CMK that is stored in the customer's EU KMS partition. Session keys are rotated every 15 minutes by default; explicit revoke endpoint exists for emergency deprovisioning. Rotation uses AEAD envelopes and never exports raw key material.
- Egress: The private deployment is peered to Aurelius' EU VPC via a PrivateLink endpoint. All outbound egress for model inference traffic is routed through the peered EU NAT/GW; control-plane telemetry is pushed to our EU control plane region and retained within EU boundaries for the customer. The attached VPC map labels peering endpoints and CIDRs.
- SOC2/SIG note: The bridge letter confirms that key backups are stored in the customer's EU KMS partition only (no cross-border backup). Where customers opt into Redwood-managed backups, those backups can be geo-restricted on request — see the runbook section 3.

Attachments (zip contents listed):
- 2027-01-31-ephemeral-kms-runbook.pdf (2 pages) — TTLs, rotation flowchart, emergency revoke, API snippets.
- vpc-egress-map-aurora-eu.png — annotated network diagram with peering endpoints and egress CIDRs.
- soc2-bridge-letter-aurelius.pdf — 1-page attestation for SOC2/CAIQ use.

If this covers your acceptance criteria, please confirm and we'll send a signed PDF of the bridge letter. If you need HSM-specific wording, we can add an HSM appendix by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
